author: GamingBolt
description:
Toy Story 3 Complete Edition is a conservative upgrade of a solid, beloved diamond in the rough. It is, of course, also a welcome surprise, because a remaster of the Toy Story 3 licensed game wasn’t really something that anyone was expecting (or, truthfully, hoping for). 

Though it still has the original experience's flaws and isn’t quite as comprehensive as its name suggests, Complete Edition is a fun, charming, delightful platformer that fans of the Toy Story universe and platforming experiences in general will surely enjoy.
title: Toy Story 3: Complete Edition Review - Nostalgia Overload?

author: GamingBolt
description:
I don't think the reception from some fans means Max Payne should stay in his miserable lane forever, or even the core impetus for the remakes. Maybe its lack of success (if you believe Take-Two at the time) is due to other factors. Perhaps the world was over Max Payne. Maybe it expected something else entirely from Rockstar and wasn't willing to put down $60, especially with so many other big games that year. It could even come down to marketing or the lack thereof.

As the man himself said, “Things had a habit of only making sense to me looking back, long after I'd run out of time to fix them.” Regardless of the reason, Max Payne 3 still stands out as an incredible action game, and no, not with the caveat of being a bad Max Payne game. Opinions will always vary, but just as there's room for remakes that could fundamentally alter everything we loved about the originals, there's also space for a Max who finds some solace at the end of it all.
title: Was Max Payne 3 Really A Failure?

author: GamingBolt
description:
Phantom Blade Zero might be selling its combat quite enthusiastically ahead of its release, but that doesn’t mean that the rest of the game is any less significant to the experience it aims to present us with. The Wulin, or the Phantom World, is equally important as the stage that allows the entire adventure to unfold.

As such, it fills a role that’s as important as the gameplay, and we think it’s going to surpass the expectations it carries, and perhaps rival Soul himself in terms of how memorable it can be. Why is that? As always, the answers are long and nuanced. Join us as we dive into what we think about a world that could have us firmly settled in until we’ve teased out every little secret it holds.
title: Phantom Blade Zero - Why Its World Could Be Just as Engaging as Its Combat
